content: To apply for the position of Editor-in-Chief, please send an email expressing your interest in serving as an Editor-in-Chief, Associate Editor-in-Chief, Assistant Editor-in-Chief, or Contributor for a specific topic or microchapter. Make sure to attach your CV and/or a biographical sketch. Dr. D., a Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, is the founder and current Editor-in-Chief of the WikiDoc site. You do not need to hold the title of Editor-in-Chief to edit content on the site. However, you must be logged in to make edits. It is possible to have more than one Editor-in-Chief for a specific topic or subtopic. You can choose to be an editor of a microchapter rather than being responsible for all the content related to a disease state. You may also apply to be an Associate Editor-in-Chief for a subtopic. Please email your interest and attach your CV and/or biographical sketch. Healthcare professionals who are experts in a specific topic are encouraged to apply for the position of Editor-in-Chief. Fellows are encouraged to apply for the role of Associate Editor-in-Chief, while interns, residents, and students should apply for the position of Assistant Editor-in-Chief. You can serve as Editor-in-Chief for more than one page. To qualify as an expert, you should have publications such as textbooks or manuscripts relevant to the topic. Priority is given to original, peer-reviewed publications. Clinical experts with an extensive list of review articles are also eligible. At present, C.D. from Harvard Medical School is responsible for appointing Editors-in-Chief. You will be notified of your appointment via email. The term of appointment is one year. Your term will be automatically renewed if your page meets the standards of WikiDoc. However, WikiDoc reserves the right not to renew your appointment if you fail to make significant contributions or if the content does not meet the required standards. WikiDoc may also rotate the responsibility of Editor-in-Chief for a page at its discretion. As an Editor-in-Chief, you are expected to contribute original material or edit existing content related to your topic. You must monitor the page to ensure the validity of any materials added. In addition to ensuring accuracy, you must also ensure that the content remains free of bias. On your user page, you are required to disclose any real or perceived conflicts of interest related to your topic(s), including but not limited to research funding, consultancies, and honoraria. You can post this information on your user page, which can be created by typing User:Your Name (using your real name, such as Bob Smith) in the search box. This will create a new page where you can add biographical material, disclosures, your phone number, and your email address. To monitor the page you are responsible for, click the watch button at the top of the page. You will receive email alerts whenever changes are made to the page. The criteria for becoming an Associate Editor-in-Chief are similar to those for Editor-in-Chief but are less stringent and focused on a specific subtopic. Chief residents or fellows can qualify for this role, and other individuals may qualify depending on their level of training and expertise. All allied health professionals, including students, nurses, interns, and residents, are eligible to apply for the position of Assistant Editor-in-Chief. An individual can serve as Editor-in-Chief, Associate Editor-in-Chief, or Assistant Editor-in-Chief of a microchapter without being responsible for the content of all other pages related to the disease state. If you do not wish to hold the title of Editor-in-Chief or any similar title, you can still edit pages. If you are uncomfortable with the title of Chief, you can be listed as a contributor instead, if you prefer.
